standard.title: Topic and technical vocabulary
standard.description: extend topic-specific and technical vocabulary and know that words can have different meanings in different contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students experiment with and begin to make conscious vocabulary choices to suit a topic (AC9E2LA09). They have not yet examined how topic-specific and technical vocabulary works across disciplines, or how words shift meaning across contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students extend topic-specific and technical vocabulary and understand that words can have different meanings in different contexts.

nodes.label: Topic-specific and technical vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use topic-specific and technical vocabulary for their learning area topics, including measurement terms and narrative terms.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and use at least three technical or topic-specific words from a learning area topic and explain what each means in that context.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and use technical words for specific topics across the curriculum — e.g. metric length terms, narrative feature terms (character, setting, plot); extend vocabulary by adding prefixes and suffixes to known words.
wider: Compare technical vocabulary from two different subject areas (e.g. maths and science) and discuss how each subject builds its own specialised vocabulary
Investigate how adding a prefix or suffix to a word creates new vocabulary with related but different meaning

response_modes.reason: Vocabulary extension is inherently repertoire-based — students need to encounter and use topic-specific words repeatedly across different topics and subject areas to build a genuinely expanding vocabulary. Range across learning areas is the growth mechanism.

success_criteria: Student uses at least two topic-specific or technical words accurately in context
Student can explain what each word means in that learning area context

nodes.label: Words with different meanings in different contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify words that have different meanings in different contexts and explain how the context determines which meaning is active.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one word that has different meanings in different contexts (e.g. 'warm' in everyday vs scientific contexts) and explain what it means in each context.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and explore words that have different meanings in different contexts — everyday meanings versus technical meanings — and use context clues to determine which meaning is active.
wider: Find examples of the same word used in an everyday context and a subject-specific context in the same week of learning, and discuss how they know which meaning is intended
Explore how new words enter a topic vocabulary and what happens to the everyday word when a technical term takes over the same meaning

response_modes.reason: Students often assume a word has one meaning. Seeing the same word used differently across contexts — maths vs everyday, science vs everyday — reveals that meaning is context-dependent. Multiple contrast examples are necessary for this insight.

success_criteria: Student identifies a word with multiple meanings and names at least two contexts
Student explains what the word means in each context and how they know which applies
